clue.text: Take these for healthy diet and exercise

definitions.text: Take these for healthy diet and exercise

parts.words: Take these for healthy diet and exercise
parts.note: two kinds of fruit make a healthy diet, and in cockney rhyming slang the same phrase means stairs, which you take for exercise

explanation.surface: Advice to eat well and keep fit.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang uses this fruit phrase for 'stairs', so 'take these ... for exercise' means climbing the stairs, while the fruit itself is the healthy diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Two common fruits suit a healthy diet, and the rhyming-slang sense is the stairs people climb for exercise.

clue.text: County set up exchange to restrict last of currency

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the reversed word closes around a letter
in a down clue, set up means the word is written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: to swop (a variant of swap) is to exchange

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A county council arranges a currency exchange with limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses SWOP to POWS, and 'to restrict' puts Y, the last letter of 'currency', inside it. POWYS is a county in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Powys is a Welsh county, so it is an example of the general term.

clue.text: Design philosophy misses out in collective wisdom

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the word for collective wisdom

parts.note: lore is the traditional knowledge held by a group

indicators.note: out signals the letters of misses are knocked out of place and rearranged

explanation.surface: A design philosophy is omitted from a body of shared knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'misses out' meaning omits, but it signals the anagram; 'in' makes the container. The motto is linked with the architect Mies van der Rohe.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimalist motto, associated with the architect Mies van der Rohe, is a principle of design.

clue.text: Frozen course sounding painful on horse

indicators.note: sounding signals that the words that follow are to be said aloud

parts.note: painful is sore, and a bay is a horse, so this phrase is sore bay, which sounds like the frozen dessert

explanation.surface: A course in riding that hurts as you sit on the horse.
explanation.walkthrough: SORE (painful) followed by BAY (a reddish-brown horse) sounds like 'sor-bay', the way SORBET is often said.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorbet is an iced dessert or palate cleanser served as one course of a meal.

clue.text: Where returning astronauts stay cool and dry with not a soul about

indicators.note: about means the phrase for not a soul goes around the word for dry

parts.note: not a soul means no one
sec is the French word for dry, used of wines

explanation.surface: Space travellers coming back to Earth keep calm, and stay sober with nobody around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cool' is part of the definition, not a synonym to find: the nose cone is the heat-shielded front of a craft re-entering the atmosphere. 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose cone is the protective front section of a spacecraft, shielding the crew from the heat of re-entry.

clue.text: No work left in profit

indicators.note: in means the letter for left is put inside the word for profit

parts.note: pay is earnings, a profit from work

explanation.surface: Not working, so no wages earned.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreation is the opposite of labour, so the leisure activity means no work.

clue.text: Having rows with man/ego/man, order columns for Greek king

indicators.note: writing the three words as rows of a grid and reordering the columns rearranges their letters

explanation.surface: An instruction for laying out a page of text in rows and columns.
explanation.walkthrough: Write MAN, EGO and MAN as three rows; the columns read MEM, AGA and NON. Order them AGA, MEM, NON to get the king's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the king of Mycenae who led the Greeks against Troy in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Drunk wants stupid ads describing rough pub

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger about and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunk wants silly adverts describing a rough bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' signals an anagram of WANTS STUPID ADS. A spit-and-sawdust pub is a basic, rough one, from the old practice of sawdust on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a basic, unrefined bar, from the sawdust once strewn on floors to soak up spills.

clue.text: Give clumsy actor a hand on collected episodes where a reasonable man may be found

definitions.text: where a reasonable man may be found

parts.note: to give a hand is to applaud, to clap
a ham is an actor who overacts
an omnibus edition collects several episodes of a programme

explanation.surface: Applaud a poor actor appearing in a compilation of episodes of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give ... a hand' is applause, CLAP. In English law the 'man on the Clapham omnibus' is the ordinary reasonable person; Clapham is a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: English courts use the man on this London bus as the standard of an ordinary, sensible person.

clue.text: Wife wearing welcome gifts from Hawaiian part of island

indicators.note: the wife wears the garlands, so they go around her letter

parts.note: leis are flower garlands given as a welcome in Hawaii

explanation.surface: A wife is wearing garlands given as a welcome in Hawaii.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts W inside LEIS: LE-W-IS. Lewis is the northern part of the Scottish island of Lewis and Harris.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis forms the northern portion of Lewis and Harris, the largest island of the Outer Hebrides.

clue.text: Autocrat recalled from a distance, one who inspires dread?

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the word for autocrat is written backwards

parts.note: a tsar is an absolute ruler
afar means from far away
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dictator remembered from far off is someone who causes fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns TSAR into RAST. Ras Tafari, later Haile Selassie, is revered by Rastafarians, many of whom wear dreadlocks: he inspires 'dread', not fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Haile Selassie, born Ras Tafari, is the figure behind the Rastafari movement whose followers wear dreadlocks.

clue.text: Simple steps in change for epidemic disease

indicators.note: in means the word for simple steps goes inside the word for change

parts.note: pence are coins, small change
a stile is a simple set of steps over a fence

explanation.surface: Easy dance steps that change to cope with an outbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' looks like an anagram signal, but here it means coins; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestilence is a deadly plague spreading widely through a population.

clue.text: Eastern river in western 'arbour

indicators.note: in an across clue, western means written from right to left, so backwards

parts.note: harbour with its H dropped, cockney style, is haven with its H dropped

explanation.surface: A river in the east flows into a western harbour, said in a dropped-h accent.
explanation.walkthrough: A haven is a harbour; drop the H as the apostrophe in ''arbour' does, giving AVEN, and 'western' reverses it. The Neva flows through St Petersburg.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neva is the Russian river running through St Petersburg into the Baltic.

clue.text: English exhibition centre, less refined in tendency for confusion

indicators.note: in means the English and exhibition-centre pieces go inside the word for tendency

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination

indicators.note: less means the letter for refined is taken away

parts.note: a museum is a place where exhibits are shown
U is the abbreviation for upper-class, so refined

explanation.surface: An English show venue, rather less posh, in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes U from MUSEUM, giving MUSEM; with E it goes 'in' BENT: B-EMUSEM-ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemusement is the state of being puzzled or bewildered.

clue.text: Winged women's title: sirens?

parts.note: alar means having wings, from Latin ala, a wing
Ms is a title for a woman

explanation.surface: A title for winged women, asking whether they are the Sirens of myth.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the winged Sirens of Greek myth, but the sirens here are warning signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirens are warning devices that sound alarms, so the noun works for them.

clue.text: Sound recording's "gold" semiconductor mostly consists of carbon

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: mostly means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a diode is a semiconductor device
consists of is read as is, as in is made of
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A gold record, made with a semiconductor chip, consists largely of carbon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts DIODE to DIOD. A gold disc is also the music industry award, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An audio disc, such as a CD or vinyl record, stores sound.

clue.text: A new dune, shifting and sucking

indicators.note: a dune shifts with the wind, so its letters move around

explanation.surface: A fresh sand dune is moving and drawing things in.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby not yet weaned still feeds by suckling.

clue.text: Online experts enjoy period with computing on the rise

parts.note: dig is slang for enjoy
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: in a down clue, on the rise means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: IT, information technology, is computing

explanation.surface: Enjoy an era in which computing is booming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rise' turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: The digerati are people expert in digital technology and the internet.

clue.text: Perhaps I reduced to clear my good fellow

definitions.meaning: 1-across is apples and pears, perhaps produce, and produce cut in price to clear it is past its best
a dated British form of friendly address to a man

explanation.walkthrough: The '1' refers to 1-across, APPLES AND PEARS, examples of fruit; stale produce is marked down to clear it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop produce marked down for clearance is stale, and the phrase is also an old-fashioned British term of endearment between men.

clue.text: Eu gain wasted old money

indicators.note: wasted means the letters are ruined and rearranged

explanation.surface: Gains from the European Union squandered on old currency.
explanation.walkthrough: A guinea was an old British coin worth 21 shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: The guinea is a former British coin, a unit of currency no longer minted.

clue.text: Many tricks involving alternate parts of loom in weaving race

indicators.note: involving means the word for many tricks surrounds the other letters

parts.note: in bridge a slam is winning all or nearly all of the tricks

indicators.note: alternate parts means every other letter of the word is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Lots of tricks with a weaving loom in a textile contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Take L and O from LOOM and put them inside SLAM: SLA-LO-M.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiers or canoeists weave between gates in this timed race.

clue.text: Beginner among 18 with advantage in hindsight

indicators.note: in hindsight means looking back, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: a boon is a benefit or advantage

explanation.surface: A novice among online experts, with the advantage of looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is 18-down, DIGERATI: a noob is internet slang for a newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: Noob is gamers' and online slang for an inexperienced newcomer.

clue.text: Very skilled splice catches young fishes biting line

indicators.note: catches means the word for splice holds the rest inside it

parts.note: to splice is to join, informally to marry, to wed

indicators.note: biting means the young fishes close their jaws around the letter for line

parts.note: elvers are young eels

explanation.surface: Joining a fishing line captures small fish that bite it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splice' means marry here, an informal sense; 'biting' and 'catches' are nested containers, the line going inside the young fish first.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well versed in a subject means being thoroughly knowledgeable and practised in it.

clue.text: Concerted attack as hairdresser's possibly closing early, around five

indicators.note: around means the shortened shop name is placed around the numeral
closing early means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a hairdresser's is one kind of salon
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A hairdresser's shuts early around five, to the customers' fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closing early' cuts SALON to SALO, and 'around' puts V inside: SAL-V-O.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, a combined assault.

clue.text: Seabird's skull, all devoid of lines

indicators.note: devoid of means the letters for lines are removed from both words

parts.note: the two words as written
L is the abbreviation for line, so lines here are a pair of Ls in each word

explanation.surface: A seabird's skull, with every line gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove LL from both SKULL and ALL to leave SKU and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The skua is a large predatory gull-like bird of the sea.

clue.text: Does it need pointing out, to get through this impenetrable barrier?

definitions.text: Does it need pointing out, to get through this impenetrable barrier?

parts.words: Does it need pointing out, to get through this impenetrable barrier?
parts.note: pointing is the mortar work on masonry, and an obstacle you cannot get through needs no explaining

explanation.walkthrough: Pointing is filling the joints in brickwork with mortar; the clue also plays on 'talking to a wall' when the point does not get through.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall of bricks is a solid obstacle, and figuratively an obstacle nothing can get past.

clue.text: Few bullies regularly masked evil spirit

indicators.note: every other letter is hidden behind a mask, leaving the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A handful of bullies, disguised at intervals, are wicked spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of FEW BULLIES are E, B, L, I and S. Eblis is the chief devil in Islamic tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eblis, or Iblis, is the devil figure of Islamic belief.

clue.text: Marks to be acquired by doctors I teach in such a "questionable" way?

definitions.text: Marks to be acquired by doctors I teach in such a "questionable" way?

indicators.note: questionable means dubious, so the letters are put into doubt and rearranged

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Doctors who teach by constant questioning earn good marks for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange M plus DOCTORS I TEACH. The Socratic method teaches by asking questions, hence 'questionable' in quotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates taught by putting questions to his pupils, a dialectic method of teaching.
